validation.notes:
The PBEEE programme page (frq.gouv.qc.ca/en/program/merit-scholarship-program-for-foreign-students-pbeee-2026-2027-2/) carries no FRQ logo image at all: the header renders the org name as text ('
Fonds de recherche du Quebec
') and the only image there is the Quebec government mark. I therefore followed the official brand page for the same publisher, frq.gouv.qc.ca/le-fonds-de-recherche-du-quebec/mention-visibilite-logo/, whose 'Logo officiel' section publishes the full-size colour PNG (1034px wide) as a direct download link. I downloaded the file and viewed it: it is the 'Fonds de recherche Quebec' wordmark with the Quebec fleur-delise flag, i.e. the genuine official FRQ logo. Identity match: the record's official_source is the Fonds de recherche du Quebec, the same organisation that publishes this logo, so identity is exact. Rejected: /app/themes/webit/favicon-32x32.png, /app/themes/webit/favicon-16x16.png, /app/themes/webit/apple-touch-icon.png, /app/themes/webit/safari-pinned-tab.svg (all favicon/mask icons), /app/themes/webit/assets/img/logo-qc.png (that is the Quebec *government* signature, a different organisation from FRQ), /app/uploads/2023/10/logo_ees.jpg (an unrelated partner/agency logo embedded in body copy), /app/themes/webit/assets/img/wave--mixed.svg (decorative hero art), the pastille PNGs (social-media roundel reserved for social use per the brand guide), and the Wikimedia Commons 'LOGO_FRQNT_720X720.png' (third-party mirror of the pre-2024 FRQNT brand).

validation.notes:
No official ANRF logo image exists on the official domain. I fetched https://www.anrfonline.in/ANRF/Ramanujan_fellowship, which served the ANRF site (title 'The Electronic Project Proposal Management System, For ANRF'). I read the entire returned HTML and enumerated every image reference. The ANRF site lockup in the header is pure text, not an image: '
...
Anusandhan National Research Foundation
'. The only images on the page are: /ANRF/resources/app_srv/serb/gl/homepage_new/images/homepage/img/cadc.png (alt='cdac logo' - the unrelated Centre for Development of Advanced Computing logo in the footer), user.svg (login UI icon), and chrome/mozilla/edge/safari.png (browser UI icons), plus a data:image/png;base64 Facebook 1x1 tracking pixel. There is no ANRF logo asset, no brand/media page and no downloadable brand asset on anrfonline.in. The only public traces of an ANRF logo are LinkedIn/X posts (Sept 2025 'the official logo ... is currently under development'; a new logo 'unveiled ... at ESTIC2025'), which the contract rejects as social-media evidence and which I therefore cannot use to prove an official asset. Official absence beats fake branding, so image_url stays null.

validation.notes:
This is the strongest candidate available: the programme's own logo, published on the official scholarship page for this exact record. The first element of the page content is , placed immediately above the page heading

Convocatoria extraordinaria 2026

, which matches the record title verbatim. I downloaded the 988x454 PNG and viewed it: it is a clean wordmark reading 'Beca Generacion del Bicentenario' in white type on a magenta/pink speech-bubble lozenge. That is a logo, not decorative hero art, and it matches the record identity exactly. It is not a favicon, UI chrome, a social avatar, a mirror, a screenshot or a tracking pixel. PRONABEC's institutional wordmark (https://www.pronabec.gob.pe/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Pronabec-Logo-2020.png, 380x73, blue 'PRONABEC' with a multicolour rule) is a valid official-provider fallback and is recorded here as examined, but the programme logo is preferred under the contract's source hierarchy (official scholarship/programme page first).

validation.notes: The record's official_source is the United Negro College Fund, and UNCF publishes no separate logo for the Etta Gray Memorial Scholarship. The official UNCF brand mark on the official scholarships page is the site header/footer logo: . I downloaded the SVG and inspected it: 387x223.2, Adobe Illustrator export, fills #FFFFFF, #FDB917, #F68B33, i.e. the UNCF initials with the torch in UNCF yellow/orange. It is the genuine official logo, on the official domain (uncf.org, not a mirror), and is not a favicon, UI icon, social avatar or screenshot. Two caveats drive MEDIUM rather than HIGH: (1) it is the white reverse variant intended for UNCF's dark header, so the white portions will be low-contrast on a light page background; (2) I could not locate any official UNCF brand-asset or media-kit page offering a full-colour or black downloadable version, so this is the only provable official asset. Both are presentation concerns, not provenance concerns, hence recovered rather than not_found. Rejected: https://uncf.org/wp-content/uploads/favicon.png and the cropped-favicon-32x32/180x180/192x192/270x270 variants (favicons), https://cdn.uncf.org/wp-content/uploads/va_union_graduation_banner-1920.jpg (og:image photograph banner, not a logo), and https://cdn.uncf.org/wp-content/uploads/2026-LA-MB-Sponsorship-92.pdf (a sponsorship booking form, not a brand-asset page).

validation.notes: Same provider, same official asset as record 632. On the official Frederick Douglass Bicentennial Scholarship Program page the only brand mark is the UNCF site logo: in the footer, with alt="UNCF - A Mind is a Terrible Thing to Waste" in the header and off-canvas menu. The page's own imagery is photographic, not a logo: the primary image is (an 800x450 banner photograph), plus gallery photographs fdouglass_03-forever-free-400.jpg, 2020-douglass-winner-800.jpg and fdouglass-scholarship-group-800.jpg. Those are decorative programme photography, not a logo, so they are rejected. UNCF publishes no separate Frederick Douglass programme logo and no official brand-asset page with a full-colour or black logo file, so the white reverse header logo is the only provable official asset; MEDIUM for the same two presentation caveats as record 632 (white reverse variant for dark backgrounds; no official colour brand asset exists), not for provenance.
